Thanks for the heads-up. A few security constraints and recommendations from my side:

- BYOK/SSE-KMS: We currently support server-side encryption with our KMS for hosted buckets. Customer-supplied KMS for direct S3 buckets is not fully automated in our hosted plane — current path requires a Dedicated/Private deployment or an ops-assisted key binding (manual). We can offer temporary escrow of encrypted blobs with customer-provided public key while we land a proper BYOK flow.

- Network delivery: direct HTTPS push to external endpoints must use mutual TLS + client cert rotate and should be restricted to destination allowlists. For Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) we commonly recommend an ingress proxy in the customer's VPC or S3 staging as the simpler option.

- PII redaction & schema: we can add a sanitization layer to the audit export pipeline to replace sensitive text with deterministic SHA256 hashes and include a redaction_flags field. This will require a small change to the enrichment lambda (estimate: 2–3 engineer-weeks including tests).

- Retention: 7-year retention for raw events is heavy; suggest offering: full-fidelity (7 years) behind a Reserved / Dedicated contract OR default: 90 days full + aggregated rollups for long-tail. If Orchid requires 7 years of raw events, this should be scoped as an enterprise compliance add-on with cost/ops implications.

I'll add our policy doc on encryption/workflow here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-orchid-telemetry-spec

Jonas
